author: product-requirements-expert
title: Correct a booked visit's date and description
summary: A booked visit can be corrected in place: its date and its description can be changed under the same rules that govern booking, and the pet gains no second visit. Nothing links to the correction this round.
acceptance_criteria: given a booked visit, when its correction is opened, then that visit's current date and description are shown ready to be changed
given a new description and a date later than today, when the correction is submitted, then that visit carries both and the owner's record is shown
given an accepted correction, when the pet's visits are counted, then the count is unchanged
given a blank description or a date of today or earlier, when the correction is submitted, then it is refused, the field is named, and the form is shown again
given a visit whose date has already passed, when it is corrected, then the date must also move later than today (PRD Visits edge case 3)
non_goals: cancelling or withdrawing a booked visit (NG-5), and deleting one (NG-4)
a visible entry point: no page links to the correction in this round, and the owner detail page gains no link; a later request may add one
changing which pet or owner a visit belongs to — only the date and the description are correctable
notes: ADR need for design triage: the 2026-08-08 non-goal ADR (docs/adr/2026-08-08-non-goal-deletion-and-visit-amendment.md) decides that "a booked visit is immutable" and requires that narrowing NG-5 later carry "its own non-goal ADR". The NG-5 narrowing of 2026-08-12 makes that ADR partly stale; a superseding or amending non-goal ADR is needed. This dispatch reserved docs/adr/ to system-design-expert, so the PRD-side change was made here and the ADR is left for design triage to raise. Note the project's adr-template skill assigns non-goal ADRs to product-requirements-expert, so triage may route it back rather than author it. Owner-fixed constraints carried from intake, for the design stage to place: the correction is addressed at the booked visit's own address under its owner and pet, suffixed "/edit", and it reuses the existing visit form and its visit model attribute. Two open questions were recorded in the PRD rather than decided here, per the owner's standing instruction: whether a visible entry point should exist, and whether a correction addressed to the wrong owner or pet is refused (booking refuses that case; nothing states that correction does). The narrowest reading was taken on both.

scope_overrides.owner_decision: Cancelling a booked visit stays out of scope; correcting a booked visit's date and description is now in scope.

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: Correcting a booked visit reuses the nested-edit-under-the-aggregate pattern PetController already demonstrates. The address is /owners/{ownerId}/pets/{petId}/visits/{visitId}/edit, GET and POST, on the existing VisitController; the aggregate entry point stays Owner and the write path stays OwnerRepository.save, per system-design.md Overview and Contracts (the 'Invariants the rows cannot carry' paragraph). The adjustment is confined to VisitController's shared @ModelAttribute("visit") method: it becomes conditional on an optional visitId path variable, exactly as PetController.findPet is conditional on an optional petId (PetController.java:75-87). No new package, type, dependency, or persistence shape.
integration_points: VisitController gains GET and POST /owners/{ownerId}/pets/{petId}/visits/{visitId}/edit; the booking routes at .../visits/new are untouched

loadPetWithVisit takes @PathVariable(name = "visitId", required = false) Integer visitId; when it is null the current behaviour stands (new Visit, pet.addVisit), when it is present it returns the existing Visit found in pet.getVisits() and adds nothing
Pet gains a getVisit(Integer id) lookup mirroring Owner.getPet(Integer id) (Owner.java:117), so the collection walk stays on the type that owns the collection rather than in the controller

the correction POST writes through this.owners.save(owner) — the same single write path the booking POST uses (VisitController.java:109); saveAndFlush is not needed because there is no integrity violation to catch
the template is reused unchanged: form th:object="${visit}" posts to the current URL, and visit['new'] is false on the correction path so the heading drops 'New'

patterns.description: optional path variable on a shared @ModelAttribute method, letting one lookup serve both the create and the edit mapping in one controller
in-place child update: resolve the existing child from the aggregate by id, apply the changed fields to it, save the root
the booking handler this one mirrors: @Valid on the model attribute, controller date check, redirect to the owner record on success, form view on error

risks.risk: IN-PLACE UPDATE — the sharpest failure mode. pet.visits is a Set<Visit> mapped @OneToMany(cascade = ALL) @JoinColumn("pet_id") (Pet.java:56-59), and Visit inherits no equals/hashCode (BaseEntity defines none), so set membership is identity-based. Any freshly constructed Visit added to that set is a second element with a null id, which the cascade turns into an INSERT — the pet gains a second visit. The current @ModelAttribute method constructs and adds one on every request in the controller (VisitController.java:78-79), so an unguarded edit mapping fails this criterion by default.
risks.mitigation: On the correction path resolve the existing Visit out of pet.getVisits() by visitId and return that instance from the @ModelAttribute method, calling neither new Visit() nor addVisit. Spring binds the form onto that same instance, its id is non-null, and owners.save(owner) cascades a merge that Hibernate resolves to an UPDATE of the existing row. Identity-based hashing means mutating date and description does not disturb set membership, so the element count is unchanged. Do not copy PetController's copy-the-fields variant here: binding straight onto the aggregate's own instance is what keeps the count fixed.

risks.risk: Duplicating the non-future-date check into a second controller method adds a business rule to a web controller. architecture-principles.md line 91 states that a new rule in a controller is a fresh violation not covered by the recorded deviation, and its checklist bars it outright.
risks.mitigation: Extract the existing check (VisitController.java:100-102) into one private helper and call it from both handlers, keeping the controller's rule count at one and adding no new rule. Reuse the existing typeMismatch.visitDate error code. Moving the rule onto the domain — a bean-validation constraint on Visit.date — is the principled fix, is broader than this slice, and is recorded below as an open question.

risks.risk: Binding onto a persisted entity makes identifier tampering directly harmful: an id form field would repoint the update at another row. system-design.md Threat Model records the binder disallow-list as the standing mitigation for mass assignment.
risks.mitigation: Leave the existing @InitBinder setDisallowedFields("id", "*.id") (VisitController.java:51-54) in place and unmodified. The visit identity comes from the path only.

risks.risk: A correction addressed to a visitId that does not belong to the pet in the path, or to the wrong owner or pet. The PRD records this as an open question; booking already refuses the wrong-pet case.
risks.mitigation: Narrowest reading: refuse it the same way loadPetWithVisit already refuses an unknown pet (VisitController.java:71-74) — throw IllegalArgumentException naming the identifiers. This is a same-shape rejection, not a new policy. It surfaces on the error page, whose message rendering is an existing Known Defect; only identifiers are exposed, no secret.

risks.risk: Blank description is enforced by @NotBlank on Visit.description (Visit.java:42) via @Valid, not by a controller check. Adding a controller-side blank check would be a fresh violation of the Web controller row.
risks.mitigation: Rely on @Valid and the existing binding result; assert the field error in the test rather than adding a check.

risks.risk: Two concurrent corrections of the same visit: Visit carries no @Version, so the later write wins silently.
risks.mitigation: Accepted, consistent with the application's existing posture — no entity in this codebase carries optimistic locking. Recorded here rather than fixed; out of scope for this slice.

risks.risk: THE STALE NON-GOAL ADR IS A SLICE-BLOCKING DOC OBLIGATION. docs/adr/2026-08-08-non-goal-deletion-and-visit-amendment.md still decides that 'a booked visit is immutable' and its Consequences require that narrowing either row later carry its own non-goal ADR. The PRD's NG-5 row cites that record as pending. The slice must not close with the PRD citing a pending record.
risks.mitigation: Routed back to product-requirements-expert — see notes for the assigned owner, the decided form of the record, and the required content. This is a product record, not an architectural one; the design side of the narrowing is settled by this design-block.

notes:
ADR OWNERSHIP AND FORM — decided here, authored elsewhere. The record is a non-goal ADR, and both the adr-template skill and docs/adr/README.md line 56 assign non-goal ADRs to product-requirements-expert, whose write scope matches docs/adr/*-non-goal-*.md; the infix is called load-bearing there. I do not author it. Routing should dispatch product-requirements-expert to write it before this slice closes. The FORM is decided here, because choosing between supersession and amendment is a record-keeping judgement rather than a product one: write a NEW non-goal ADR, do not supersede the 2026-08-08 one. Rationale — that ADR decides two rows, and only half of one is narrowed: NG-4 stands untouched, the cancellation half of NG-5 stands, and only the amendment half changes. Its own Consequences prescribe exactly this ('its own non-goal ADR'). Required content: filename docs/adr/2026-08-12-non-goal-visit-correction-narrows-ng-5.md; Status Accepted; the Decision states that correcting a booked visit's date and description is in scope while cancelling and deleting remain out; a sentence recording that the 2026-08-08 sentence 'a booked visit is immutable' no longer holds as written; Implementation section '**Non-goal:** NG-5'; back-links to the PRD Non-Goals and to the 2026-08-08 ADR. Add a forward pointer in the 2026-08-08 ADR's prose so a reader of the stale sentence is redirected — its Status stays Accepted, because the README's Status values offer no partial-supersession token and the record remains accurate for NG-4 and for cancellation. Update the PRD's NG-5 row to cite the new ADR instead of a pending record, and add the new row to the docs/adr/README.md index. NOT A CONFLICT: the 2026-08-08 ADR itself provides the escape hatch — 'A future request touching either row proceeds only on an explicit owner decision recorded at intake' — and the prd-entry carries that decision as a scope_overrides entry with source 'dispatch'. The override used the prescribed mechanism, so the verdict is minor rather than conflicting; what remains is the recording obligation the ADR imposes.

DOC-SYNC OBLIGATIONS, after the code lands. docs/system-design.md states in its provenance banner that every statement describes what the code demonstrably does, so it is deliberately not updated ahead of implementation. Three edits are then due: the VisitController Contracts row's Purpose extends from booking to booking and correction, and its Implements gains REQ-VIS-003; the Visit and OwnerRepository rows' Implements gain REQ-VIS-003; the State Machine section's sentence about pet workflows branching on the persisted test extends to the visit workflows. Naming them here so the obligation is not lost between the design-block and doc-sync.

OPEN QUESTIONS RECORDED, per the standing owner instruction — no consultation-request raised. (1) Whether the non-future-date rule belongs on the domain as a bean-validation constraint on Visit.date rather than in the controller. Deferred: it would change the booking path's error code and behaviour, which is REQ-VIS-001 ground, and it is broader than this slice. (2) Whether a correction addressed to the wrong owner or pet should be refused; the narrowest reading above matches booking's existing refusal. (3) Whether a visible entry point should exist; out of scope this round per the prd-entry non_goals, and the template therefore needs no new link.

VOCABULARY. docs/ubiquitous-language.md has no term for correcting a booked visit, and 'Visit' currently lists 'Booking' under Avoid while the PRD and this slice both use 'booked'. Flagged for product-requirements-expert, who owns that file; not written here, since this is not a foundational triage.

IMPLEMENTER NOTES. The test that guards the count criterion should assert against the Owner instance the mocked OwnerRepository returns, or capture the argument passed to save, and read pet.getVisits().size() from it — the controller mutates that in-memory graph, so the assertion is direct. The existing @WebMvcTest fixture (VisitControllerTests.java:59-66) needs a persisted-looking Visit with a non-null id added to the pet. The template's 'Add Visit' button label comes from the addVisit message key; if a correction-specific label is introduced, REQ-LANG-002 and I18nPropertiesSyncTest require the new key in all eleven bundles, so the narrowest reading is to leave the label alone. Basis for the covering-pattern claims above: direct reads of the named source files, the IDE oracle not being connected in this run.

the booking handler this one mirrors: @Valid on the model attribute, controller date check, redirect to the owner record on success, form view on error

risks.risk: IN-PLACE UPDATE — the sharpest failure mode, carried forward from line 4 unchanged. pet.visits is a Set<Visit> mapped @OneToMany(cascade = ALL) @JoinColumn("pet_id") (Pet.java:56-59) and Visit inherits no equals/hashCode, so set membership is identity-based. Any freshly constructed Visit added to that set is a second element with a null id, which the cascade turns into an INSERT. The current @ModelAttribute method constructs and adds one on every request (VisitController.java:78-79), so an unguarded edit mapping fails the count criterion by default.
risks.mitigation: On the correction path resolve the existing Visit out of pet.getVisits() by visitId and return that instance from the @ModelAttribute method, calling neither new Visit() nor addVisit. Spring binds the form onto that instance, its id is non-null, and owners.save(owner) cascades a merge Hibernate resolves to an UPDATE. Identity-based hashing means mutating date and description does not disturb set membership, so the element count is unchanged. Do not copy PetController's copy-the-fields variant; binding straight onto the aggregate's own instance is what keeps the count fixed.

risks.risk: Duplicating the non-future-date check into a second controller method adds a business rule to a web controller. architecture-principles.md line 91 states a new rule in a controller is a fresh violation not covered by the recorded deviation.
risks.mitigation: SHARED DATE-VALIDATION HELPER — extract the existing check (VisitController.java:100-102) into one private helper called from both handlers, keeping the controller's rule count at one and adding no new rule. Reuse the existing typeMismatch.visitDate error code.

risks.risk: Binding onto a persisted entity makes identifier tampering directly harmful: an id form field would repoint the update at another row. system-design.md Threat Model records the binder disallow-list as the standing mitigation for mass assignment.
risks.mitigation: Leave the existing @InitBinder setDisallowedFields("id", "*.id") (VisitController.java:51-54) in place and unmodified. The visit identity comes from the path only.

risks.risk: A correction addressed to a visitId that does not belong to the pet in the path, or to the wrong owner or pet. Recorded as an open question in the PRD, not decided.
risks.mitigation: Narrowest reading: refuse it as loadPetWithVisit already refuses an unknown pet (VisitController.java:71-74) — throw IllegalArgumentException naming the identifiers. Same-shape rejection, not a new policy. Only identifiers are exposed, no secret.

risks.risk: Blank description is enforced by @NotBlank on Visit.description (Visit.java:42) via @Valid. A controller-side blank check would be a fresh Web-controller violation.
risks.mitigation: Rely on @Valid and the existing binding result; assert the field error in the test.

risks.risk: Two concurrent corrections of the same visit: Visit carries no @Version, so the later write wins silently.
risks.mitigation: Accepted, consistent with the codebase's existing posture — no entity carries optimistic locking. Recorded, not fixed; out of scope.

author: security-reviewer
recommendations: Not verified against the NVD: the OWASP dependency-check plugin is not configured in build.gradle and this review has no network access, so no CVE match was run. The resolved framework floor is unchanged by this diff (Spring Boot 4.1.0 via the plugin, io.spring.dependency-management 1.1.7). A human or CI closes this check; it is stated as not run, not as clean.

Pre-existing, replicated rather than introduced: processVisitCorrectionForm takes @ModelAttribute Owner owner, which resolves the repository-loaded Owner from the model and then data-binds request parameters onto it before owners.save(owner). A crafted POST to the correction URL carrying firstName/lastName/address/city/telephone rewrites the owner's contact details as a side effect of correcting a visit. The identifier is protected by the disallow list, and processNewVisitForm has had exactly this shape since before the change, so the change is not weaker than the baseline and NG-1's no-authorization posture means the same actor may already edit the owner directly. Worth narrowing in a later pass (bind the visit alone and re-read the owner for the save) so the sample does not teach binding-onto-a-persisted-aggregate as the idiom.

A visitId that does not belong to the pet currently surfaces as a 500 error page rather than a 404. The refusal is correct and leaks nothing; the status code is a presentation question. The PRD already records the underlying open question ('Is a correction addressed to the wrong owner or pet refused?'), so this is a note for whoever answers it, not a defect in this change.
approved_aspects: Identifier binding stays disallowed on the correction path: VisitController's @InitBinder is byte-for-byte untouched by the diff and still reads setDisallowedFields("id", "*.id"). This is what makes binding onto a persisted Visit safe — a request parameter id=<other> cannot repoint the bound entity's primary key, and *.id blocks the nested case on the co-bound Owner graph. All three controllers (Owner, Pet, Visit) carry the same disallow list, so the correction path adds no divergence (security-principles Mass assignment row: safe state is the default, not remembered per-endpoint).

Cross-pet and cross-owner identifier tampering is refused by construction. VisitController.loadPetWithVisit resolves owner -> pet -> visit strictly through the aggregate: owners.findById(ownerId), then owner.getPet(petId) (walks that owner's pets only), then the new Pet.getVisit(visitId) (walks that pet's visits only, and its !visit.isNew() guard prevents a transient null-id visit from ever matching). A visitId belonging to a different pet resolves to null and the request is refused before any binding or save occurs. Verified against Owner.java:117 and Pet.java:87.

The refusal's information disclosure is bounded. The IllegalArgumentException message interpolates only int/Integer path variables, so no request-supplied text reaches it — no log injection and no reflected content. It is not rendered to the client either: error.html renders ${message} with th:text (escaped), and server.error.include-message is unset in application.properties, so Spring Boot's default of never leaves it blank. The message shape also matches the pre-existing owner-not-found and pet-not-found refusals in the same method (Pattern Consistency).

Cross-request state is re-validated, not trusted. Both the GET and the POST re-resolve the whole owner/pet/visit chain from the repository on every request; nothing is carried in session or trusted from a prior request (security-principles Trusting cross-request state row).

Validation is not weakened on the correction path. The extracted rejectDateNotInFuture applies the identical future-date rule to booking and correction, and @Valid still enforces @NotBlank on description. On a rejection the mutated entity is not persisted: spring.jpa.open-in-view=false leaves the loaded graph detached, so there is no dirty-check flush behind the error return.

No new attack surface classes: no shell execution, no file or path handling, no deserialization, no query-string concatenation, no new logging, and no new controller-level mutable state on the singleton bean. Templates render every value through th:text with escaping on; no th:utext and no Thymeleaf preprocessing were introduced.
Supply chain unchanged: build.gradle is not in the change set, so no new dependency was added and the four dependency checks do not apply to this change.

title: Correct a booked visit's date and description
summary: A booked visit can be corrected in place: its date and its description can be changed under the same rules that govern booking, and the pet gains no second visit. Nothing links to the correction this round.
acceptance_criteria: given a booked visit, when its correction is opened, then that visit's current date and description are shown ready to be changed
given a new description and a date later than today, when the correction is submitted, then that visit carries both and the owner's record is shown
given an accepted correction, when the pet's visits are counted, then the count is unchanged
given a blank description or a date of today or earlier, when the correction is submitted, then it is refused, the field is named, and the form is shown again
given a visit whose date has already passed, when it is corrected, then the date must also move later than today (PRD Visits edge case 3)
non_goals: cancelling or withdrawing a booked visit (NG-5), and deleting one (NG-4)
a visible entry point: no page links to the correction in this round, and the owner detail page gains no link; a later request may add one
changing which pet or owner a visit belongs to — only the date and the description are correctable

author: security-reviewer
recommendations: If a future slice ever retires NG-1 and introduces authentication, revisit all three refusal messages in VisitController.loadPetWithVisit together: at that point the owner/pet/visit not-found messages become a cross-tenant enumeration oracle and the identifier echo stops being free. The test added in this round pins the message content, so that future change will surface here rather than passing silently.
approved_aspects: No production change since the round-1 basis: the fix-delta against review-plan basis tree aa11050 contains only docs/adr/2026-08-08-non-goal-deletion-and-visit-amendment.md, docs/system-design.md, docs/ubiquitous-language.md, and src/test/.../VisitControllerTests.java. Pet.java and VisitController.java are byte-identical to the tree I approved in round 1, so the round-1 security verdict carries forward unchanged.

Mass-assignment control intact: VisitController.setAllowedFields still calls dataBinder.setDisallowedFields("id", "*.id") at VisitController.java:51-54, unchanged in the delta. Identifier binding stays disallowed on both the booking and the correction POST, satisfying the Mass assignment row of docs/security-principles.md.

The new test theVisitCorrectionFormShouldBeRefusedWhenTheVisitIsNotOneOfThePets weakens no control. It adds no permissive test configuration, no security-config override, and no stub that lets a request bypass loadPetWithVisit; it drives the real MVC dispatch through MockMvc and asserts only that the ownership refusal propagates. It is a pure addition of negative coverage over the visit-not-found branch.

Identifier echo in the refusal message is acceptable under this project's NG-1 posture, and locking it into a test does not change that view. Both identifiers the message names are caller-supplied path variables echoed back, not server-held state: an unauthenticated caller learns only that the visitId it just typed is not one of the petId it just typed. Under NG-1 (docs/prd.md:39 - no accounts, sign-in, or restriction on who may read or change records) there is no confidentiality boundary for that fact to cross; the same caller can read the owner detail page and enumerate the real visits directly. The message carries no credential, connection string, or session identifier, so the Secret disclosure through logs and errors row of docs/security-principles.md is satisfied. Both path variables are declared int/Integer, so a non-numeric probe fails path conversion before reaching the message - the echo cannot become a reflected-XSS vector on the error page that renders the exception text.

Pattern consistency held: the visit-not-found refusal at VisitController.java:92-93 uses the same shape as the pre-existing owner-not-found and pet-not-found refusals in the same method. The class sweep over loadPetWithVisit found no divergent third form of the same concern.

assertThatThrownBy(...).rootCause().isInstanceOf(IllegalArgumentException.class).hasMessageContaining(...) is the right shape here, not a pinned implementation detail. No @ExceptionHandler exists anywhere in src/main (grep confirms zero @ControllerAdvice/@ExceptionHandler in the app), so an unresolved exception in a @WebMvcTest genuinely propagates through MockMvc.perform as a wrapped exception -- there is no HTTP-status contract to assert against instead (the round-1 security-reviewer record independently noted this same gap: an unmatched visitId currently surfaces as a 500, and the status code is an open PRD question, not a defect of this diff). rootCause() is also the more defensive choice over a single getCause() hop: it survives a change in servlet-exception wrapping depth. The two hasMessageContaining assertions on the visit id and pet id are the real behavioral contract under test and match the design-block's decided mitigation verbatim ('throw IllegalArgumentException naming the identifiers').

author: change-grader
summary: correct a booked visit in place

blast_radius.note: Two production files in one package, one module, no sensitive paths; six of the nine changed files are docs. The one wide edit is the shared @ModelAttribute loadPetWithVisit, which every visit endpoint including the pre-existing booking flow passes through, and the four original booking tests are unchanged and still green.

semantic_surprise.note: Read every hunk. The Set-plus-cascade double-insert is genuinely closed by the visitId == null guard, Pet.getVisit is scoped to the pet and skips unsaved visits, and the untouched Thymeleaf form carries no action attribute so it self-posts to whichever mapping rendered it, which is why no template change was needed. The residuals are understood and deliberate: an unknown visitId raises IllegalArgumentException out of the model-attribute method, so a wrong id surfaces as a 500 rather than a 404, and the correction form still reads Visit over an Add Visit button. Binding mutates the loaded Visit before validation can reject it, which is inert here because spring.jpa.open-in-view=false leaves the aggregate detached and no save runs on the rejection path.

test_adequacy.note: The MVC tests are real rather than tautological: they drive the actual dispatch, binding and validation, assert on the domain object's own state, and cover blank description, a today date, a visit whose date has already passed, and a visitId belonging to no visit of this pet. But the owner's sharpest requirement is a persistence claim and it is tested only against a @MockitoBean OwnerRepository. containsExactly(bookedVisit) proves the in-memory graph and verify(owners).save(owner) proves save was called; neither proves the detached merge cascades an UPDATE rather than an INSERT through Pet's cascade-ALL visits collection. ClinicServiceTests is a @DataJpaTest that already holds shouldAddNewVisitForPet and gained no correction counterpart.

reviewer_hedging.note: All four dispatched reviewers approved round 2 with empty findings, but two of those approvals carry recommendations lists and the code-quality-reviewer's approval explicitly parks its round-1 clarify finding as open by design: rejectDateNotInFuture removes the duplication but keeps the date rule in the controller, taking the recorded Form-validator migration from one call site to two. The security approval defers a review of all three refusal messages to any future slice that introduces authentication. Three product questions were recorded rather than decided.

scope_deviation.note: The production surface is exactly the two correction mappings the requirement names. The NG-5 narrowing, its new non-goal ADR, and the forward pointer in the 2026-08-08 ADR are the sanctioned record of an explicit owner decision rather than creep, and the prior ADR correctly stays Accepted as a narrowing not a supersession. Two design revisions and three PRD rewrites converged before implementation, with zero build retries and zero consultations. Worth knowing: the PRD still lists the wrong-owner-or-pet refusal as an open question while the diff pins a specific answer to it in a test.

rationale: The duplicate-visit failure mode is genuinely closed, and the conditional lookup, the in-place binding and the self-posting form all read correctly. But no-second-visit-record is a persistence claim proved only against a mocked repository; the @DataJpaTest that already covers booking gained no correction counterpart. Confirm the cascade emits an UPDATE.
